title: Choose PostgreSQL as the source of truth for Beacon
context: Beacon needs durable storage for tenants, projects, and audit records while the team is still small.
decision: Use PostgreSQL as the transactional source of truth and keep schema changes in versioned migrations.
alternatives: Use SQLite for the first release
rationale: PostgreSQL provides relational constraints, familiar operations, and transactional queries for tenant isolation.
consequences: Read replicas can be added later

title: Adopt Redis streams for asynchronous event delivery
context: Webhook delivery and report generation must not block Beacon API requests during traffic spikes.
decision: Use Redis streams with consumer groups for short-lived asynchronous jobs.
alternatives: Publish directly from the API process
rationale: Redis is already operated for caching, and streams provide acknowledgements without introducing a second platform.
consequences: Failed jobs require a retry policy

title: Move tenant authorization into the policy service
context: Authorization checks were duplicated across API handlers and diverged when new project roles were introduced.
decision: Centralize tenant and project authorization in a policy service called Gatekeeper.
rationale: A policy service gives every caller the same role semantics and creates one auditable decision point.
consequences: API calls add a bounded network hop

title: Replace Redis streams with managed queue delivery
context: The Redis stream backlog during the July incident delayed customer webhooks and competed with cache memory.
decision: Move durable asynchronous jobs to the managed CloudQueue service while retaining Redis for cache data.
alternatives: Keep Redis streams with shorter retention
rationale: CloudQueue separates durable job storage from cache memory and provides managed retry and dead-letter queues.
consequences: Webhook latency is easier to monitor

title: Beacon transactional data model and API
problem_statement: Beacon needs consistent tenant-scoped storage and CRUD APIs for projects and audit records.
architecture: A stateless API writes to PostgreSQL through a repository layer; every tenant-owned table includes tenant_id.
technical_requirements: Enforce tenant_id on reads and writes
tradeoffs: Relational joins simplify reporting but require index ownership

title: Asynchronous webhook delivery worker
problem_statement: Webhook delivery must retry transient failures without holding API requests open.
architecture: The API publishes a job, workers deliver webhooks with exponential backoff, and failed jobs remain inspectable.
tradeoffs: Redis reduces platform count but couples cache and durable jobs

title: Gatekeeper policy service integration
problem_statement: Inconsistent authorization logic allowed some project role changes to bypass the intended policy.
architecture: The API sends a signed subject, tenant, resource, and action to Gatekeeper, which returns an allow or deny decision.
technical_requirements: Cache decisions for at most 30 seconds
Log policy version with every decision
tradeoffs: Central consistency adds latency and an availability dependency

title: Webhook backlog caused delayed customer notifications
impact: Customer webhooks were delayed by up to 47 minutes and 3.2 percent of deliveries exceeded their retry window.
root_cause: Redis stream retention and cache keys competed for memory, causing worker restarts and a growing unacknowledged stream.
resolution: Operators increased capacity, paused nonessential consumers, and replayed the affected delivery range after stabilizing Redis.

title: Project role update bypassed authorization check
impact: One tenant's project administrator could update a project member role without the required owner permission; no cross-tenant data was exposed.
root_cause: The role-update handler used a legacy inline check that did not include the new ownership constraint.
resolution: The endpoint was disabled briefly, the missing policy was deployed, and affected audit records were reviewed.

title: Migration lock delayed the morning deployment
impact: The deployment was delayed for 28 minutes while a long-running reporting query held a PostgreSQL migration lock.
root_cause: The migration runner used an unrestricted lock wait and did not detect the reporting query before applying a table change.
resolution: The query was cancelled, the migration completed, and the release proceeded with no data loss.
preventive_actions: Move heavy reports to a replica

title: Operational observability and incident response
problem_statement: The July webhook incident showed that queue age and delivery delay were not visible before customers reported symptoms.
architecture: Services emit structured metrics and traces to the telemetry gateway; alerts link directly to runbooks and document IDs.
technical_requirements: Preserve document IDs in alert annotations
tradeoffs: More telemetry costs storage but shortens diagnosis time

title: Use read replicas for reporting workloads
context: Reporting queries can hold locks and consume primary database resources needed by transactional API traffic.
decision: Route eligible reporting queries to a PostgreSQL read replica with an explicit freshness budget.
alternatives: Tune every report on the primary
Move reporting to a separate warehouse
rationale: A replica reduces immediate operational risk while preserving the existing relational model and a future warehouse path.
consequences: Reports may lag by up to five minutes
